description: A neighborhood web app for finding little free libraries (book-swap boxes on porches), seeing what is inside, adding and removing books, leaving check-in notes, and reporting problems. Made-up example idea used to demonstrate PlanForge.

sections.title: App Architecture Framework
sections.overview: A small server-rendered web app with a thin JSON API, built as one deployable. Maps and book lookups are the only heavy parts, so everything else stays boring.

decisions.choice: Next.js 15 (App Router) as a single full-stack app
decisions.rationale: One repo, one deploy, SSR for shareable library pages.

decisions.choice: Leaflet + OpenStreetMap tiles instead of Google Maps
decisions.rationale: No API key or billing for a hobby-scale app.

implementation.repo_structure: single package: app/, lib/, db/, tests/
implementation.state_management: React Server Components + TanStack Query for the map view
implementation.rendering_strategy: SSR for library pages, client component for the map

risks.risk: Leaflet is client-only and breaks SSR
risks.mitigation: Load the map with next/dynamic ssr:false

agent_notes: Keep all map code in components/map/ so it can be swapped later.

sections.title: Database Setup
sections.overview: PostgreSQL with PostGIS-free simple lat/lng columns and bounding-box queries, enough for a neighborhood-scale app.

decisions.choice: PostgreSQL 16 via Drizzle ORM
decisions.rationale: Typed queries and simple SQL migrations.

id, library_id, user_id, note, created_at
id, library_id, reporter_id, reason, resolved

implementation.indexing_strategy: Index on libraries(lat,lng), books(library_id) where removed_at is null, checkins(library_id, created_at desc)
implementation.migration_strategy: drizzle-kit generate, migrations committed and run on deploy

risks.risk: Bounding-box queries slow down at scale
risks.mitigation: Move to PostGIS if libraries exceed ~50k rows

agent_notes: Soft-delete books with removed_at; never hard delete.

sections.title: Server Requirements
sections.overview: One small VPS runs the app and the database behind nginx.

decisions.rationale: Plenty for a few thousand users and cheaper than managed services.

critique.summary: Buildable hobby-scale monolith, but five personas converge on the same weak spots: abuse and authorization are intent, not enforced rules; mail, storage and staging config contradict across server, integrations and environment; and the deploy mechanics (pm2 reload with a symlink swap) don't work as written. Security is the harshest scorer (5) because ownership checks, upload hardening and rate limiting are too thin to ship.

issues.issue: Authorization is page-level only. No server-side role or ownership checks; any member can edit any library's books; hide/ban capabilities have no routes or status values.
issues.recommendation: One requireRole/requireOwnerOrAdmin helper on every mutating handler; define libraries.status and users.status enums; add IDOR and role-escalation tests.

issues.issue: Auth.js database sessions need adapter tables and users has no role column; Auth.js email provider is SMTP-based while integrations specifies the Postmark SDK.
issues.recommendation: Add adapter tables and a role column; send mail through Postmark SMTP relay via SMTP_URL; use a POST confirm page so email scanners cannot burn the link.

issues.issue: In-memory rate limiter resets on deploy, is per-process, keys login on victim email only, and sees 127.0.0.1 for every request behind nginx.
issues.recommendation: Postgres-backed limiter, per-IP and per-email login limits, daily email cap, nginx X-Real-IP trust, Turnstile on login and /add.

issues.issue: Upload pipeline and CSP are under-specified: no magic-byte check, pixel limit, random keys, scoped bucket key; CSP missing script/connect directives and Sentry host.
issues.recommendation: Magic-byte validation, sharp limitInputPixels, UUID keys, PutObject-only scoped key, upload-only body limit, nonce-based CSP with full directive set, never accept photo_url from clients.

issues.issue: Env var list omits Postmark/S3/Sentry secrets, and staging has no topology (port, database, vhost, bucket) despite environment and deployment promising it.
issues.recommendation: Complete the env var list; define staging as a second pm2 app on 3001 with its own database, vhost behind basic auth and S3 prefix; add to budget.

issues.issue: pm2 reload plus symlink swap keeps running the old release in fork mode, migrations run against live schema, no server-side dependency install, no health-gated rollback.
issues.recommendation: Next.js standalone output, ecosystem.config.js with explicit cwd and startOrReload, separate migration step, health check with automatic symlink revert, expand/contract migrations.

issues.issue: Acceptance criteria are untestable as written and ownership, edit, delete and hide behavior is undefined.
issues.recommendation: Rewrite criteria as Given/When/Then with numbers; add a permissions matrix; add edit/delete library, hide library and /me as MVP features.

issues.issue: No directory ownership, no DevOps agent, and the Code Auditor is read-only yet expected to block handoffs.
issues.recommendation: Directory-ownership table, add a DevOps/Release agent, give the Auditor a failing CI check as its blocking mechanism.

issues.issue: No log rotation module, no external uptime monitor, Sentry may capture PII by default.
issues.recommendation: pm2-logrotate, free external uptime monitor on /api/health, sendDefaultPii false and a beforeSend scrubber.

issues.issue: Standards are prose, not enforced; thresholds missing.
issues.recommendation: Encode as ESLint rules, set thresholds (zero madge cycles, jscpd under 3%, audit high fails, coverage gate 80%).

issues.issue: Overview says four pages but there are six routes; no check-email screen, no admin 404 rule, no next= redirect.
issues.recommendation: Fix the count, add missing screens, specify non-admin gets 404, add ?next= redirect.

open_questions.question: OpenStreetMap's public tile server is a best-effort service that can block app-style use. What is the map tile plan?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The map is the main feature; a blocked tile host means a blank home screen.
suggested_options: Free-tier tile provider with an API key
Self-host tiles on the existing bucket
Stay on OSM for the pilot with a config switch ready

open_questions.question: Where do backups live so a single server failure cannot take the data and its backups together?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The recovery point and location decide whether the documented restore works.
suggested_options: Encrypted dump to a separate bucket prefix with write-only key

open_questions.question: The Postmark free tier is 100 emails a month and new accounts need approval. What is the email plan?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Login gates every write feature; an email cap silently stops all contributions.
suggested_options: Pay Postmark $15 from launch and request approval in week 1

open_questions.question: Which day-one gaps are MVP: edit/delete library, denied-geolocation fallback with address search, accessible list view, photo required or optional?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Real users hit these on day one.
suggested_options: All of those in MVP, photo optional
Keep MVP minimal and document the gaps

open_questions.question: Reports and admin tooling are in the last phase but the Report feature is MVP. What is the phase order?
suggested_options: Move reports and admin into Contribute

qa_log.question: Map tile plan?
qa_log.answer: Stay on OSM for the pilot with attribution and a TILE_URL config switch so we can swap to a keyed provider without code changes.

qa_log.question: Backup location?
qa_log.answer: Encrypted nightly dump to a separate bucket with a write-only key, alert if the newest dump is older than 26 hours, restore test before launch and quarterly.

qa_log.question: Email plan?
qa_log.answer: Pay for Postmark ($15) from launch, request sender approval in week 1, daily send ceiling with an alert.

qa_log.question: Day-one MVP gaps?
qa_log.answer: Edit/delete library, denied-geolocation fallback with address search, and an accessible list view are MVP. Photo is optional. Clustering and duplicate detection wait for v2.

qa_log.question: Phase order?
qa_log.answer: Move reports and admin tooling into the Contribute phase. Launch phase is hardening only.

sections.title: App Architecture Framework
sections.overview: A server-rendered Next.js monolith with a small REST API. Map tiles come from OpenStreetMap for the pilot behind a TILE_URL switch, so a keyed provider can replace them without code changes.

decisions.choice: Next.js 15 App Router, output: 'standalone'
decisions.rationale: One deploy bundle that carries its own runtime dependencies.

decisions.choice: Leaflet with a configurable TILE_URL (default OSM) and visible attribution
decisions.rationale: OSM's tile policy allows light use with attribution but can block heavy use; the switch removes the single point of failure.

implementation.api_style: REST JSON: GET /api/libraries?bbox=, POST /api/libraries, PATCH|DELETE /api/libraries/:id, POST /api/libraries/:id/books, DELETE /api/books/:id, POST /api/libraries/:id/checkins, POST /api/reports, POST /api/uploads, GET /api/health, GET /api/geocode?q=
implementation.repo_structure: app/ and components/ (Lead Builder), db/ (Data Engineer), tests/ (QA), infra/ (DevOps), lib/ shared
implementation.state_management: Server Components plus TanStack Query for the map
implementation.rendering_strategy: SSR for library pages; client-only map via next/dynamic ssr:false

risks.risk: OSM blocks or throttles tile requests
risks.mitigation: TILE_URL switch, attribution, a custom User-Agent-friendly Referer, and a documented swap to a keyed provider

agent_notes: All map code lives in components/map/ and reads TILE_URL from config.
Every handler calls the shared auth helpers from lib/authz.ts.

sections.title: Database Setup
sections.overview: PostgreSQL 16 with explicit status enums, Auth.js adapter tables, and expand/contract migrations. Backups go off the box.

decisions.choice: Two database roles: migration owner and DML-only runtime role
decisions.rationale: A compromised app cannot alter the schema.

decisions.choice: Expand/contract migrations only
decisions.rationale: Old code must keep working against the new schema during a deploy.

schema_overview.key_fields: id, email (lowercased, unique), display_name, role enum(member,admin), status enum(active,suspended), created_at
per @auth/drizzle-adapter
id, owner_id, name, lat, lng, address_hint, photo_key, status enum(active,hidden,removed), created_at
id, library_id, isbn, title, author, added_by, removed_at
id, library_id, user_id, note, hidden, created_at

schema_overview.purpose: Reports on libraries, check-ins or users
schema_overview.key_fields: id, target_type, target_id, reporter_id, reason, resolved_by, resolved_at
key, points, expire_at
isbn, payload, fetched_at

implementation.indexing_strategy: Composite index on libraries(status, lat, lng) for bounding-box queries; books(library_id) where removed_at is null; checkins(library_id, created_at desc); plan earthdistance or PostGIS past 50k rows
implementation.migration_strategy: drizzle-kit generate; run in a dedicated deploy step by the migration role; expand/contract only
implementation.backup_strategy: Nightly pg_dump, encrypted with age, uploaded to a separate bucket with a write-only key, 30 day retention, alert if newest dump is older than 26 hours or under a minimum size, restore into a scratch database before launch and quarterly
implementation.connection_pooling: pg Pool max 10 for the runtime role

risks.mitigation: Freshness and size alert, quarterly restore drill

agent_notes: Soft-delete books and hide libraries; never hard delete in handlers.
Account deletion anonymizes check-ins and removes the email.

sections.title: Server Requirements
sections.overview: One VPS runs production and a gated staging side by side, behind nginx, with a complete env var list.

decisions.choice: Staging as a second pm2 app on the same VPS
decisions.rationale: Cheapest topology; isolated by port, database, role, bucket prefix and basic auth.

implementation.cpu_ram_estimate: 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 60 GB disk (prod and staging)
implementation.nginx_config_notes: TLS via certbot; set X-Real-IP from $remote_addr; client_max_body_size 64k globally and 6m only on /api/uploads; limit_req as a coarse outer layer; HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy; staging vhost behind basic auth

env_vars_needed.purpose: Migration role, used only in the deploy step
Public photo host used in CSP
Error reporting and source map upload (CI only)

risks.mitigation: pm2 max_memory_restart on staging and a 4 GB RAM alert

agent_notes: Bind everything except nginx to 127.0.0.1.
Run the app as a non-root app user; deploy user has sudo only for pm2 reload.

sections.title: Environment Strategy
sections.overview: Dev, staging and prod each have separate databases, buckets and secrets, with approval before prod.

decisions.choice: Server-side env files plus GitHub environment secrets for CI
decisions.rationale: Small team; no secret manager needed yet.

implementation.env_file_strategy: .env.local for dev; /etc/porch-library/env and /etc/porch-library-staging/env, mode 600, owned by the app user; .env.example lists every key
implementation.secrets_management: Files on the server; CI deploy key scoped to the deploy user; rotation runbook per secret (AUTH_SECRET rotation logs everyone out, which is acceptable)
implementation.promotion_process: Merge to main deploys staging; prod tag requires GitHub environment approval

sections.title: Features
sections.overview: Find nearby libraries, view and change contents, and moderate. Criteria are written as Given/When/Then with numbers and a permissions matrix.

decisions.choice: Photo optional, edit/delete and accessible list view in MVP
decisions.rationale: Real users need to fix mistakes and use the app without the map.

mvp_features.name: Browse map
mvp_features.description: Pins within the viewport; center defaults to the device location, else a typed address, else the pilot neighborhood
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given the 20-library seed and throttled 4G, when the page loads, then first pins render in under 3 s; given geolocation is denied, then an address search box is shown and the map centers on the default; results capped at 200 pins per request

mvp_features.name: Nearby list view
mvp_features.description: Accessible text list of the same results, keyboard navigable
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given any map view, when the list tab is opened, then libraries are listed by distance and each is reachable by keyboard

mvp_features.name: Library page
mvp_features.description: Photo, address hint, current books
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given a library with 60 books, when opened, then the first 50 show with a Load more control

mvp_features.name: Add a library
mvp_features.description: Member picks a point on the map, names it, optionally adds a photo
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given a logged-in member, when they submit valid data, then it appears on the map within one refresh; given a library within 20 m, a duplicate warning is shown

mvp_features.name: Edit or delete my library
mvp_features.description: Owner or admin edits fields or removes it
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given I am the owner, when I delete, then status becomes removed and the public page shows the gone page

mvp_features.name: Add or remove a book
mvp_features.description: ISBN lookup or manual title and author
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given a member, when they add a book, then it shows after the server confirms; only the adder, the library owner or an admin can remove it

mvp_features.name: Check-in note
mvp_features.description: Leave a note
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given a member, a note up to 280 characters shows newest first

mvp_features.name: Report
mvp_features.description: Report a library, check-in or user
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given a member, when they report, then it appears in /admin/reports

mvp_features.name: Moderation
mvp_features.description: Admin hides a library, deletes a check-in, or suspends a user
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given an admin action, then the target is hidden for public users and the action is logged

mvp_features.name: My page and account deletion
mvp_features.description: /me lists my libraries and check-ins and lets me delete my account
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given I delete my account, then my email is removed and my check-ins are anonymized

future_features.name: Wishlist alerts
future_features.description: Notify when a wanted title appears

risks.mitigation: Owner may set an approximate location and use a takedown path

sections.title: Authentication
sections.overview: Passwordless magic links through Auth.js with server-side authorization on every mutating handler.

decisions.rationale: One mail path, standard tables.

sections.title: 3rd-Party Tools & APIs
sections.overview: Postmark SMTP, an S3-compatible bucket, Open Library, OpenStreetMap tiles, a geocoder and Turnstile.

decisions.choice: Photos are uploaded to our server, re-encoded with sharp, then written to the bucket
decisions.rationale: Required to strip EXIF and validate content.

integrations.name: Open Library
integrations.rate_limits: Polite use; 24 h cache in isbn_cache

integrations.name: OpenStreetMap tiles
integrations.fallback_strategy: Swap TILE_URL to a keyed provider

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.overview: Postgres-backed rate limits keyed on the real client IP, strict upload handling, nonce-based CSP, and authorization on every write.

decisions.choice: Postgres-backed rate-limiter-flexible
decisions.rationale: Survives restarts and works across cluster workers.

rate_limiting.tool: rate-limiter-flexible with Postgres store plus nginx limit_req
rate_limiting.limits: Login 5/hour per email and 10/hour per IP; new accounts 3/day per IP; writes 30/hour per user; uploads 10/hour per user; reads 300/min per IP; global EMAIL_DAILY_CAP

implementation.input_validation: zod on every handler with max lengths (name 80, note 280, address_hint 120, title 200); photo uploads validated by magic bytes, 5 MB, sharp limitInputPixels 24 MP, 10 s timeout, EXIF stripped
implementation.csp_headers: Nonce per request via middleware: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-…' ; connect-src 'self' plus Sentry ingest host; img-src 'self' tile host and PHOTO_PUBLIC_BASE; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'
implementation.xss_prevention: React escaping, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, escaped OG tags
implementation.csrf_protection: SameSite=Lax plus Origin check on writes
implementation.dependency_audit_tool: npm audit (high fails CI) plus Dependabot

risks.risk: Spoofed client IP defeats IP limits
risks.mitigation: App trusts X-Real-IP only from 127.0.0.1; integration test asserts distinct IPs count separately

agent_notes: Sentry sendDefaultPii false with a beforeSend scrubber for cookies, headers and bodies.

critique.summary: Much stronger than round 1: every round-1 contradiction is resolved, and scores held at 6 only because the council now finds second-order problems. Remaining HIGH items are mechanical: the deploy rollback does not match how pm2 behaves, the CSP blocks the Turnstile widget the login depends on, Next.js standalone output omits static assets, a single 4 GB box is exposed to out-of-memory kills, and the Code Auditor still cannot enforce anything because nobody defines which identity posts its status. Note: the Ops persona ran three web searches this round (OSM tile policy, Postmark approval, Next.js standalone with pm2); in round 1 it reported it did not search.

issues.issue: startOrReload replaces live workers before the health check, so the previous release cannot keep running; standalone output omits .next/static and public; old and new build hashes break in-flight clients.
issues.recommendation: Start the candidate on a spare port, health-check it, then flip nginx upstream; copy .next/static and public into the bundle; keep one prior release's static files.

issues.issue: CSP blocks the Turnstile script and iframe; no style-src; data: missing for markers; Referrer-Policy must not be no-referrer or OSM blocks tiles.
issues.recommendation: Allow challenges.cloudflare.com in script-src, frame-src and connect-src; add style-src and data: img; set Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin; add an e2e login test under the production CSP.

issues.issue: Postgres-backed limiter writes on every read; mail-bombing a victim email can burn the global email cap and lock out real logins.
issues.recommendation: Reads limited in nginx only; per-recipient, per-IP and reserved-quota email budgets; Turnstile on every anonymous send.

issues.issue: Prod, staging, Postgres, sharp and builds share 4 GB; a memory spike can OOM-kill Postgres.
issues.recommendation: Build only in CI, add swap, systemd memory limits, sharp concurrency 1, consider staging on demand or a separate small instance.

issues.issue: Auditor cannot enforce: no identity defined for the status check, authz and zod rules are prose, section reference off by one.
issues.recommendation: Make code-audit a GitHub Actions job under branch protection; add a lint test that every app/api handler uses requireRole and zod.

issues.issue: No audit log table; account deletion semantics and foreign keys are undefined; no geocode cache.
issues.recommendation: Add audit_log, geocode_cache, uploads tables; define deletion as a transaction with tombstoned email hash and ON DELETE SET NULL.

issues.issue: List tab has no route, confirm and edit routes and admin endpoints are missing.
issues.recommendation: Add ?view=list, /login/confirm, /library/[id]/edit and the admin API endpoints.

issues.issue: lib/ and middleware have no owner; tests-before-feature deadlocks against required green CI.
issues.recommendation: Lead Builder owns lib/ and middleware; tests land in the same PR as the feature.

open_questions.question: Should first-time uploaders' photos be held for approval, or published immediately with reactive moderation?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Public images tied to home addresses carry privacy and abuse risk.
suggested_options: Hold first photos for admin approval

open_questions.question: Postmark approval is manual and login is the only way in. What is the plan B sender?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A single vendor is the critical path for all contributions.

sections.title: App Architecture Framework
sections.overview: A server-rendered Next.js monolith with a small REST API. Map tiles come from OpenStreetMap for the pilot behind a TILE_URL switch, so a keyed provider can replace them without code changes.

decisions.choice: Next.js 15 App Router, output: 'standalone'
decisions.rationale: One deploy bundle that carries its own runtime dependencies.

decisions.choice: Leaflet with a configurable TILE_URL (default OSM) and visible attribution
decisions.rationale: OSM's tile policy allows light use with attribution but can block heavy use; the switch removes the single point of failure.

implementation.api_style: REST JSON: GET /api/libraries?bbox=, POST /api/libraries, PATCH|DELETE /api/libraries/:id, POST /api/libraries/:id/books, DELETE /api/books/:id, POST /api/libraries/:id/checkins, POST /api/reports, POST /api/uploads, GET /api/health, GET /api/geocode?q=
implementation.repo_structure: app/ and components/ (Lead Builder), db/ (Data Engineer), tests/ (QA), infra/ (DevOps), lib/ shared
implementation.state_management: Server Components plus TanStack Query for the map
implementation.rendering_strategy: SSR for library pages; client-only map via next/dynamic ssr:false

risks.risk: OSM blocks or throttles tile requests
risks.mitigation: TILE_URL switch, attribution, a custom User-Agent-friendly Referer, and a documented swap to a keyed provider

agent_notes: All map code lives in components/map/ and reads TILE_URL from config.
Every handler calls the shared auth helpers from lib/authz.ts.

sections.title: Database Setup
sections.overview: PostgreSQL 16 with explicit status enums, Auth.js adapter tables, and expand/contract migrations. Backups go off the box.

decisions.choice: Two database roles: migration owner and DML-only runtime role
decisions.rationale: A compromised app cannot alter the schema.

decisions.choice: Expand/contract migrations only
decisions.rationale: Old code must keep working against the new schema during a deploy.

schema_overview.key_fields: id, email (lowercased, unique), display_name, role enum(member,admin), status enum(active,suspended), created_at
per @auth/drizzle-adapter
id, owner_id, name, lat, lng, address_hint, photo_key, status enum(active,hidden,removed), created_at
id, library_id, isbn, title, author, added_by, removed_at
id, library_id, user_id, note, hidden, created_at

schema_overview.purpose: Reports on libraries, check-ins or users
schema_overview.key_fields: id, target_type, target_id, reporter_id, reason, resolved_by, resolved_at
key, points, expire_at
isbn, payload, fetched_at

implementation.indexing_strategy: Composite index on libraries(status, lat, lng) for bounding-box queries; books(library_id) where removed_at is null; checkins(library_id, created_at desc); plan earthdistance or PostGIS past 50k rows
implementation.migration_strategy: drizzle-kit generate; run in a dedicated deploy step by the migration role; expand/contract only
implementation.backup_strategy: Nightly pg_dump, encrypted with age, uploaded to a separate bucket with a write-only key, 30 day retention, alert if newest dump is older than 26 hours or under a minimum size, restore into a scratch database before launch and quarterly
implementation.connection_pooling: pg Pool max 10 for the runtime role

risks.mitigation: Freshness and size alert, quarterly restore drill

agent_notes: Soft-delete books and hide libraries; never hard delete in handlers.
Account deletion anonymizes check-ins and removes the email.

sections.title: Features
sections.overview: Find nearby libraries, view and change contents, and moderate. Criteria are written as Given/When/Then with numbers and a permissions matrix.

decisions.choice: Photo optional, edit/delete and accessible list view in MVP
decisions.rationale: Real users need to fix mistakes and use the app without the map.

mvp_features.name: Browse map
mvp_features.description: Pins within the viewport; center defaults to the device location, else a typed address, else the pilot neighborhood
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given the 20-library seed and throttled 4G, when the page loads, then first pins render in under 3 s; given geolocation is denied, then an address search box is shown and the map centers on the default; results capped at 200 pins per request

mvp_features.name: Nearby list view
mvp_features.description: Accessible text list of the same results, keyboard navigable
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given any map view, when the list tab is opened, then libraries are listed by distance and each is reachable by keyboard

mvp_features.name: Library page
mvp_features.description: Photo, address hint, current books
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given a library with 60 books, when opened, then the first 50 show with a Load more control

mvp_features.name: Add a library
mvp_features.description: Member picks a point on the map, names it, optionally adds a photo
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given a logged-in member, when they submit valid data, then it appears on the map within one refresh; given a library within 20 m, a duplicate warning is shown

mvp_features.name: Edit or delete my library
mvp_features.description: Owner or admin edits fields or removes it
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given I am the owner, when I delete, then status becomes removed and the public page shows the gone page

mvp_features.name: Add or remove a book
mvp_features.description: ISBN lookup or manual title and author
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given a member, when they add a book, then it shows after the server confirms; only the adder, the library owner or an admin can remove it

mvp_features.name: Check-in note
mvp_features.description: Leave a note
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given a member, a note up to 280 characters shows newest first

mvp_features.name: Report
mvp_features.description: Report a library, check-in or user
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given a member, when they report, then it appears in /admin/reports

mvp_features.name: Moderation
mvp_features.description: Admin hides a library, deletes a check-in, or suspends a user
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given an admin action, then the target is hidden for public users and the action is logged

mvp_features.name: My page and account deletion
mvp_features.description: /me lists my libraries and check-ins and lets me delete my account
mvp_features.acceptance_criteria: Given I delete my account, then my email is removed and my check-ins are anonymized

future_features.name: Wishlist alerts
future_features.description: Notify when a wanted title appears

risks.mitigation: Owner may set an approximate location and use a takedown path

agent_notes: Permissions matrix: visitor read; member add and edit own; owner edit and delete own library and any book in it; admin all.

integrations.name: Open Library
integrations.rate_limits: Polite use; 24 h cache in isbn_cache

integrations.name: OpenStreetMap tiles
integrations.fallback_strategy: Swap TILE_URL to a keyed provider

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.overview: Postgres-backed rate limits keyed on the real client IP, strict upload handling, nonce-based CSP, and authorization on every write.

decisions.choice: Postgres-backed rate-limiter-flexible
decisions.rationale: Survives restarts and works across cluster workers.

rate_limiting.tool: rate-limiter-flexible with Postgres store plus nginx limit_req
rate_limiting.limits: Login 5/hour per email and 10/hour per IP; new accounts 3/day per IP; writes 30/hour per user; uploads 10/hour per user; reads 300/min per IP; global EMAIL_DAILY_CAP

implementation.input_validation: zod on every handler with max lengths (name 80, note 280, address_hint 120, title 200); photo uploads validated by magic bytes, 5 MB, sharp limitInputPixels 24 MP, 10 s timeout, EXIF stripped
implementation.csp_headers: Nonce per request via middleware: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-…' ; connect-src 'self' plus Sentry ingest host; img-src 'self' tile host and PHOTO_PUBLIC_BASE; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'
implementation.xss_prevention: React escaping, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, escaped OG tags
implementation.csrf_protection: SameSite=Lax plus Origin check on writes
implementation.dependency_audit_tool: npm audit (high fails CI) plus Dependabot

risks.risk: Spoofed client IP defeats IP limits
risks.mitigation: App trusts X-Real-IP only from 127.0.0.1; integration test asserts distinct IPs count separately

agent_notes: Sentry sendDefaultPii false with a beforeSend scrubber for cookies, headers and bodies.
